## Problem description

This puzzle, from [@OR2021trees], reads as follows:

In the illustration below, the grid consists of empty green space, dark green $2\times 2$ 'trees,' 
and restricted white areas. 
The problem is to place $55$ ($3\times 3$), $5$ ($4\times 4$), and $4$ ($5\times 5$) blocks 
on the grid while minimizing the number of trees cut. 
Overlapping even a single cell of a $2\times 2$ tree counts as cutting the entire tree.

{{< embed notebooks/cut_trees.ipynb#e1b935e1-3ad3-4b90-bfb2-eaa70e66b1fc >}}


## MIP model

#### Parameters

- $C$: set of cells of the area (grid)
- $T$: set of trees 
- $C_t \subset C$: set of cells covered by tree $t \in T$
- $K=\{1,2,3\}$: set of sizes of blocks 
- $n_k \in \mathbb{N}$: number of blocks of size $k \in K$ to place on the grid
- $B_k$: set of candidate blocks of size $k\in K$. A block $p\in B_k$ is defined as a "subgrid" of the grid; 
therefore it is defined not only by its shape, but also by the set of cells it covers.
- $B=\bigcup_{k\in K} B_k$: set of all candidate blocks

#### Variables

- $\textcolor{blue}{x}_{p} \in \{0,1\}$: takes value $1$ if and only if block $p\in B$
- $\textcolor{blue}{y}_{c} \in \{0,1\}$: takes value $1$ if and only cell $c \in C$ is covered by some block
- $\textcolor{blue}{z}_{t} \in \{0,1\}$: takes value $1$ if and only if tree $t \in T$ is cut

#### Objective function

The problem is to minimize the number of trees that are cut:

$$
\min \sum_{t \in T} \textcolor{blue}{z}_{t}
$$

subject to:

#### Constraints

- All blocks of size $k$ should be placed: 

$$
\sum_{p \in B_k}\textcolor{blue}{x}_{p} = n_k \quad \forall k \in K 
$$


- A cell of the grid can be covered at most once, 
by one of the candidate blocks:

\begin{align}
\sum_{p \in B|c \in p}\textcolor{blue}{x}_{p}=\textcolor{blue}{y}_{c} \quad \forall c \in C \\
\end{align}

- A tree is cut if one of its cells is covered by a block:

$$
\textcolor{blue}{y}_{c}\le \textcolor{blue}{z}_{t} \quad \forall c \in C_t, \; \forall t\in T
$$

in [PuLP](https://coin-or.github.io/pulp/) (CBC) and yields $13$ cut trees (marked by an X):
